question: Should Microsoft Teams officially adopt this hybrid multi-account contract—named accounts plus a legacy root/default identity—with account-scoped credentials, policies, routing, and persisted state?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but adding public config/default behavior and defining upgrade semantics for credentials and durable Teams state is a product and compatibility commitment that automated review cannot authorize.

options.title: Sponsor the current contract
options.body: Approve the established channel account model, refresh the branch onto current main, recheck compatibility-sensitive paths, and land it.

options.title: Require canonical accounts only
options.body: Ask for a doctor migration from root identity fields into `accounts.default` and remove permanent hybrid runtime behavior before merge.

options.title: Defer multi-account Teams
options.body: Close or pause the PR if maintainers do not want to support the added configuration and state-isolation surface now.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the current contract
recommendation.body: Approve the established channel account model, refresh the branch onto current main, recheck compatibility-sensitive paths, and land it.
